answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded identity registry: each agent locks a slashable stake to earn a single vote, so influence costs capital, not just CPU. A farmer wanting a thousand votes must post a thousand bonds, and detected fraud slashes the lot. Reputation flows only to scarce, long-lived stake, an ivory mark of trust, whereas fresh clones start at zero like willow shoots without history. The harbor stays safe because entry is priced and betrayal forfeits the bond: an attacker pays linear capital upfront and risks total loss, making takeover far costlier than honest participation.
